text: When you design a REST API, clear structure matters. Start by planning your endpoints carefully. Each endpoint should represent a resource, such as users or orders, and use simple, consistent names. Always return the correct HTTP status codes, like 200 for success or 404 when something is not found, so clients understand what happened. Good documentation is essential too, because developers need to know how to use your API without guessing. Finally, use versioning, for example /v1/users, so you can improve the API later without breaking existing applications. Following these practices makes your API easier to use, maintain, and trust.
